newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Virgin aims for first step to Africa carrier.
newsitem.headline: Virgin aims for first step to Africa carrier.

text.p: Britain's Virgin Group sees its bid for state-owned South African domestic carrier Sun Air as a first step towards developing a possible pan-African service, the firm said on Monday.

The carrier, once the airline of the former independent black homeland of Bophuthatswana, has been put up for sale by the South African government. Virgin, in partnership with black empowerment consortium Bhekilanga, has put in a bid.

"We see Sun Air as having a great deal of synergy between our operations and theirs. If you look at their domestic service they are far and away the best domestic carrier in South Africa with the highest level of service," David James, general manager of Virgin Atlantic in Southern Africa, told Reuters.
Flambuoyant entreprenuer and Virgin boss Richard Branson has said previously the group would be interested in expanding across Africa's emerging markets.
James said the Sun Air bid could be seen as the first step towards that goal. "It would be reasonable to say that," he said.
He added that -- should the bid be successful -- Sun Air would seek to expand its routes beyond South Africa's borders.
"We plan a significant number of things in terms of expansion, not just in South Africa but also to expand routes with Southern Africa," he said.
Virgin already has a code-sharing agreement with Sun Air.

James added that Virgin would bring its marketing expertise and human resources development to the group. With stunts like trans-Atlantic ballooning, Branson has made effective marketing a hallmark of his rapid rise to become one of the world's most famous businessmen.
The deadline for submitting pre-qualification bids for Sun Air passed last week and the process of drawing up a short-list of candidates has already begun.
An announcement from the Department of Public Affairs is expected on Thursday.
After the pre-qualification stage stage there are two further phases -- submission of non-binding offers and final offers/completion.
James said Virgin was confident it had a strong bid. "In my personal view we have put together a very credible bid package," he said.
Bhekilanga is made up of SARHWU Investment holdings, Women In Capital Growth, Bophirima Investment Holdings, NE Corp, African Renaissance Holdings and Ukhozi Investments.

One important part of the Virgin/Bhekilanga package is the role Women In Capital Growth will play in showing a commitment to promoting women in both management roles and technical positions such as engineering jobs, James said.
"We liked what they were talking about. We liked their ideas," he added.

Virgin's growth in the South African air market has been rapid. The group started flying from London to Johannesburg in October with three flights a week. This has now risen to six and will become daily from July 16.
"We have doubled in about six months. That is a measure of how successful we have been," James said.
